title: A hand-off slot that waits instead of spinning

task.text: Producers and consumers share one slot; each must wait until its guard holds.
Implement `Slot<T>`, a one-item hand-off (**guarded suspension**). Waiting must block the thread, with no polling.

items: `void put(T item)` waits while the slot is full, then stores the item. `null` throws `NullPointerException`.
`T take()` waits while the slot is empty, then removes and returns the item.
`Optional<T> take(long timeoutMs)` does the same but returns `Optional.empty()` once `timeoutMs` has really passed.
A wakeup is not proof that the guard holds: recheck it.

checks.title: put() waits while the slot is full
Three producers and three consumers finish
take(timeout) returns an item or empty
A timed take wakes when an item arrives
A wakeup with a false guard keeps waiting
A timed take keeps waiting after a wakeup

hints.text: Each operation has a guard: put needs an empty slot, take needs an item. The thread should sleep until the guard can hold, and after waking it must check again, because another thread may have got there first.

Make the methods `synchronized`, wait in a `while` loop on the guard, and call `notifyAll()` after every change of state. For the timed take, compute a deadline once and recompute the time left after every wakeup.
